name: Hot potassium carbonate (Benfield)
applications: ammonia and hydrogen plant CO2 removal
principle: Hot aqueous potassium carbonate, promoted with an amine such as DEA, absorbs CO2 and H2S at 80 to 120 degC and is regenerated by pressure reduction and steam stripping. Absorber and regenerator run at similar temperatures, so there is no lean/rich exchanger. For LNG-grade gas the HiPure variant adds a second stage with an amine solution.

process_steps.name: Sweet gas to polishing amine stage (HiPure) or downstream
Acid gas to sulfur recovery or CO2 handling

key_equipment: hydraulic turbine on rich solvent letdown

performance.metric: sweet gas CO2 at ADGAS Train 3 (plant data / simulation)
performance.basis: Benfield HiPure with carbonate stage (30 wt% K2CO3, 3 wt% DEA) and DEA polishing stage (20 wt% DEA); plant 19 ppmv, simulation 25 ppmv

source.note: Bryan Research & Engineering, Simulation of the Benfield HiPure Process of Natural Gas Sweetening for LNG Production and Evaluation of Alternatives (ADGAS Train 3, Das Island)

performance.metric: sweet gas H2S at ADGAS Train 3 (simulation / plant)

source.note: Bryan Research & Engineering, Simulation of the Benfield HiPure Process of Natural Gas Sweetening for LNG Production and Evaluation of Alternatives (ADGAS Train 3, Das Island)

performance.metric: total reboiler duty, Benfield HiPure at ADGAS Train 3
performance.basis: carbonate unit 44 Gcal/h plus DEA unit 15 Gcal/h; feed about 477 MMSCFD at 52 barg with 4.7% H2S and 2.1% CO2 as reported (source is internally inconsistent on which is which)

source.note: Bryan Research & Engineering, Simulation of the Benfield HiPure Process of Natural Gas Sweetening for LNG Production and Evaluation of Alternatives (ADGAS Train 3, Das Island)

reference_plants.capacity: about 7 Mt CO2 avoided over ten years

source.note: CINEA, BECCS Stockholm: delivering net carbon removals with clean energy

advantages: Established, with UOP as sole licensor
HiPure reaches LNG specs (below 1 ppmv H2S, 50 ppmv CO2 as the BRE paper states)
limitations: Large solvent circulation compared with activated MDEA (BRE simulates activated MDEA at roughly 43 to 49% of the Benfield rate)
Heat demand: BRE simulates a two-stage-flash activated MDEA/piperazine case 36% lower in reboiler duty
